items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I started doing these things with him. Sometimes we'd make 50 cents between us

ctx.x: As I said before, it was during the Depression and money was very scarce, and people in the ghetto gave these parties and things, and whoever was working came. And they would sell food, what is known now as Soul Food -- it's a later term. But they'd sell things like chitlins and collard greens, pig's feet and potato salad. And we always had the neighborhood chemist that would come around and mix up a beverage, mixed it in a bathtub someplace, and mixed with alcohol, and they'd come up with a vintage 1931 White…

So Herman... I don't remember exactly the first one that we got, but I started doing these things with him. Sometimes we'd make 50 cents between us, and sometimes we would make 50 cents each -- which in junior high school for us was, you know, a penny earned, a penny gained I guess! The main thing, we were having fun doing it, and we had these grown-ups that were more or less encouraging us by hiring us, and as we played these things, they would dance.
